title: Preemptive Requeue & Soft-Island: Preemption-based Burst Handling for Dedicated Pools (PRD - Proposal)
content:
TL;DR:
We propose a preemption-first burst strategy for Dedicated pools that uses short, transparent preemption ("swipes") plus a lightweight requeue mechanism and transient
"soft-islands" to give tenants predictable burst capacity without long-term overcommit or heavy eviction. The pattern favors preserving low-latency SLOs for high-priority work while allowing opportunistic bursts for elastic tenants with a bounded preempt budget.

Problem statement:
- Dedicated customers want burst capacity for occasional spikes (seasonal campaigns, promotions, CI jobs) but don’t want noisy-neighbor effects or hard evictions that break tail latency.
- Current options (hard preempt, long warm pools, permanent overcommit) either risk breaking SLOs or raise costs significantly.
- We need a mode that provides temporary headroom, quick recovery, and predictable economics while keeping tenant isolation intact.

Goals & success metrics:
- Provide a burst UX that: (a) offers fast additional capacity (within seconds/minutes), (b) caps impact on co-tenants, (c) minimizes request failures
- Metrics to evaluate: median and p99 tail latency change for all tenants during bursts (< 10% degradation target), fraction of preempted requests that are successfully requeued and completed (> 95%), burst activation latency (target < 30s), cost delta for bursted tenant (< 20% incremental cost vs baseline for short bursts)
- Workload coverage target: web-facing low-latency inference and batch scoring pipelines for bursts up to 3x baseline concurrency for up to 30 minutes

Non-goals / constraints:
- This is not a replacement for long-lived reserved capacity or a full hot-warm pool manager.
- We do not assume every model supports checkpointing of KV cache; design accounts for cache-preserving and cache-drop modes.
- No changes to customer billing model in phase 1 (billing integration TBD in later phases).

High-level design overview:
- Preemptive Swipe: a lightweight preemption primitive that asks low-priority workers to yield capacity immediately but allows a short grace window to checkpoint state where possible.
- Requeue Engine: a centralized requeue coordinator that can accept preempted in-flight requests and either reassign to a new worker, serialize to a retry queue, or return a graceful failure depending on policy.
- Soft-Island: temporary logical grouping of freed capacity (slots/nodes) that can be granted to a tenant with strict decay and reclaim rules; islands have time-limited leases and are visible to orchestration/observability as transient capacity.
- Preempt Budget & Viscosity: each tenant gets a preempt budget (micro-credits) that governs how often we will preempt their work and how easily they can be requeued — this prevents thrashing and provides cost predictability.

Detailed components:
1) Preemptive Swipe primitive:
   - Implementation: agent on each worker listens to a central control signal; on swipe, worker marks current low-priority tasks as preemptable and attempts best-effort checkpoint (if supported by model/runtime) within X ms, then signals availability.
   - Grace window: configurable (default 200ms-1000ms depending on model class).
   - Preemption levels: soft (yield, preserve KV where possible), hard (immediate kill). We prefer soft when model supports incremental checkpointing.

2) Requeue Engine:
   - Modes: immediate reassign (if island capacity available), serialized retry queue (backpressure-friendly), client-driven retry (return 429 with transparent retry hint).
   - Prioritization: maintain per-tenant priority buckets so requeue does not starve high-priority tenants.
   - Stateful handling: where KV cache is preserved, reassign attempt includes KV affinity tokens to avoid cold-start penalties.

3) Soft-Island allocation:
   - Activation: island created when policy detector sees eligible burst signal (traffic spike, scheduled event, CLI/console request).
   - Lifetime & decay: islands have time-limited leases (e.g., default 15 min) with frictional reclaim (e.g., stepwise scale-down to allow graceful handoff).
   - Isolation guarantees: islands run with network/tenant isolation boundaries; we avoid mixing islanded slots with general-purpose pool during the lease.

4) Preempt Budget & Viscosity model:
   - Budgeting: tenants buy/are allocated preempt credits daily/monthly. Credits consumed when tenant tasks are preempted; recovery rate is configurable.
   - Viscosity: adjustable parameter that reduces churn by grouping small tasks and preferring longer-running debt amortization windows.

Scheduling & policy details:
- Eligibility detector: rule engine that observes surge signals (QPS delta, queue depth, scheduled bursts) and decides island size required.
- Fairness hedge: when multiple tenants request islands, we run a short multi-tenant auction with priority weight and preempt budget cost to determine assignment.
- Fallback: if islands unavailable, system falls back to conventional queueing with progressive backpressure and detailed failure codes.

Observability & Developer UX:
- Console shows island lifecycle (created, warmed, in-use, reclaiming), preempt events timeline, requeue success rates, and cost delta estimate for the tenant.
- API returns structured retry hints (retry-after, requeue-id, warm-affinity-token) to SDKs for automatic client-friendly retries.
- Telemetry: preemption_count, requeue_success_rate, island_uptime, median_latencies_during_burst, p99_tail_change

Failure modes & mitigation:
- Thrashing (frequent small preemptions): mitigate with viscosity parameter and minimum island lease.
- Cold-start penalty when KV dropped: additive warmup window; recommend model quantization + lightweight KV snapshot hooks for best experience.
- Starvation of non-burst tenants: enforce hard isolation fences and global p99 guardrails that stop new islands if overall cluster p99 > threshold.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): run on dev clusters with test tenants; expose CLI opts to trigger islands; gather metrics for requeue success and tail latency impact. Target: 6 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta for invited customers): enable for selected Dedicated customers who opt in; instrument billing-simulation toggle. Target: 8–12 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): production-harden with billing integration, console UX, docs and SLO contract changes. Target: 3–4 months after beta depending on telemetry.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Billing model: per-credit consumption vs. usage-based premium for island time — how to keep incentives aligned?
- KV checkpointing API: what minimal primitives do we require from runtime to make soft preemptions effective across model families?
- Interaction with Dedicated tenancy policies (hard isolation vs. soft islands): do customers want operator-visible island allocations?

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Engineering: prototype Preemptive Swipe agent and Requeue Engine adapter (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 4w).
- Applied ML: define minimal checkpoint hook for Llama-style KV caches and evaluate warmup penalties (owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 6w).
- Product: draft customer-facing beta invite language + console mockups (owner: Lena Patel, ETA: 3w).
- SRE: run chaos tests to validate that islands do not regress p99 beyond threshold at scale (owner: Jamal Singh, ETA: 8w).

Notes to reviewers / roughness:
- This is a sketch to pivot away from long warm pools; design intentionally favors short-lived, visible capacity over opaque overcommit.
- Expect follow-ups on billing and a tighter definition of preemption SLOs once early telemetry is available.
- Feedback requested: (a) acceptable preempt budget recovery cadence, (b) recommended default grace windows per model family, (c) console fields that matter most to customers.

-- end of proposal --
